questions.question_text: Simplify $\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^{-1}$, giving your answer as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Ignored the index $-1$ and copied the fraction unchanged.
Inverted the fraction but also carried the minus sign from the index into the answer.
Read the $-1$ as a minus sign on the fraction instead of an instruction to take the reciprocal.

questions.question_text: Simplify $\left(\frac{5m}{n}\right)^{-1}$, writing your answer with positive indices.

options.why: Swapped only the pronumerals and left the coefficient $5$ in the numerator.
Moved the numerator down without bringing the denominator up.
Inverted correctly but carried the minus sign from the index into the answer.

questions.question_text: Simplify $\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^{-2}$, giving your answer as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Squared the fraction without inverting it first.
Inverted the fraction but never applied the index $2$.
Inverted and squared correctly but carried the minus sign from the index into the answer.

questions.question_text: Simplify $\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^{-4}$, writing your answer with positive indices.

options.why: Raised each part to the power $4$ without inverting the fraction first.
Applied the index to the denominator only after inverting, leaving the other part to the first power.
Treated the negative index as putting the whole fraction in a denominator instead of inverting it.

questions.question_text: Simplify $\left(\frac{3x}{7}\right)^{-2}$, writing your answer with positive indices.

options.why: Squared every factor without inverting the fraction first.
Inverted and squared but did not square the coefficient $3$.
Squared the numbers but left the pronumeral $x$ to the first power.

questions.question_text: Simplify $\left(\frac{2m^{3}}{n^{4}}\right)^{-3}$, writing your answer with positive indices.

options.why: Cubed every factor without inverting the fraction first.
Inverted and cubed the pronumerals but did not cube the coefficient $2$.
Added the outside index $3$ to each inside index instead of multiplying.

questions.question_text: Simplify $\left(\frac{9t^{4}}{6t^{2}}\right)^{-2}$, writing your answer with positive indices.

options.why: Simplified inside and squared but never inverted the fraction.
Inverted the simplified fraction but applied the index as if it were $-1$.
Squared the coefficients but left the index of $t$ unchanged after inverting.

questions.question_text: Simplify $\left(\frac{3a}{b}\right)^{-2}\times\frac{9a^{3}}{b}$, writing your answer with positive indices.

options.why: Did not square the coefficient $3$ when inverting, leaving $\frac{b^{2}}{3a^{2}}$.
Squared the bracket without inverting it, so both factors stayed the same way up.
Subtracted the indices of $b$ the wrong way round, giving $b^{1-2}$ instead of $b^{2-1}$.

questions.question_text: Simplify $\left(\frac{x^{-3}}{y^{6}}\right)^{-2}$, writing your answer with positive indices.

options.why: Left the $x$ term in the denominator instead of moving it up when its index became positive.
Raised each part to the power $2$ without inverting the fraction first.
Treated the outer negative index as putting the whole expression in a denominator instead of inverting it.
